title: Law Lake tornado: Sentinel-2 canopy change (revised baseline)
summary: Sentinel-2 before/after composites show spectral change near the documented 2025 Law Lake tornado. A dual-index rule marks AOI-wide exploratory canopy-change candidates, including scattered changes away from the documented event corridor. The widened 42-day baseline, seasonal change and possible residual haze/colour or contrast differences limit attribution; this is not a complete tornado footprint.

methods.title: Quality-screened satellite composites
methods.description: Sentinel-2 harmonized surface reflectance with matched Cloud Score+ cs_cdf ≥0.65, SCL vegetation/bare classes and consistent 20 m support. Daily mosaics are reduced to bandwise reflectance medians; at least two distinct clear dates per accepted cell. RGB is a composite, not one contemporaneous photograph.

methods.title: Explicit revised experiment
methods.description: The original 6–26 July baseline failed forest coverage. V2 predeclared 15 June–26 July, keeping 28 July–17 August comparison, quality/count/coverage floors and exploratory index criteria unchanged. Earlier summer observations increase phenology and time-mixing confounds. Original-window count and support rasters are retained.

methods.title: Exploratory dual-index diagnostic
methods.description: Study WorldCover2021 mapped-tree cells with observed baseline NDVI ≥0.60. Candidate requires before-minus-after NDVI ≥0.15 AND NIR/SWIR NBR decrease ≥0.10. Report all nine sensitivity combinations. NBR here is a spectral index, not calibrated burn severity or wind-damage class.

methods.title: Observability limits
methods.description: Inspect actual before/after RGB before interpreting the AOI-wide candidate, which includes scattered off-corridor changes. Broad spectral shifts, possible residual haze/colour or contrast differences, moisture, phenology and other disturbance can explain change. NTP contextual evidence supports observability but is not an independent pixel-level validation; no surveyed track is invented. Optional per-date area aggregation failed remotely, while retained per-cell counts/date rasters and mandatory gates were audited.

methods.title: Frozen export and independent audit
methods.description: Original Colab selection, numerical manifest, processing receipt and provider audit remain byte-identical with unapproved history. Independent local checks rerun full numerical TIFFs. The portable source package retains those inputs; the website ships durable PNGs and hashed records. No credentials or live Earth Engine tile URLs are used.

limitations: Exploratory satellite observations, not independently validated damage, an official affected-area total or an emergency warning. Blank/excluded pixels are unknown, not unchanged.

Shared observations cover 93.14% of the box; baseline mapped-forest coverage is 93.22%, and shared coverage of the NDVI-qualified eligible population is 99.995%. Unobserved or excluded land is unknown, not undamaged.

The 42-day baseline mixes earlier summer conditions with a 21-day comparison; broad NDVI shifts and possible residual haze/colour or contrast differences limit interpretation. 65.76% of candidate area relies on the added earlier baseline (34.24% also has qualified original-window support). Nine-threshold candidate sensitivity is 17.1–248.0 ha, not a confidence interval.

The original baseline failed. V2 revised dates once using coverage diagnostics only; its quality/count/coverage/index thresholds were retained. Source history is preserved rather than re-labelled as approved.
This is satellite-observed spectral change near a documented tornado, not confirmed canopy-loss fraction, treefall, structural damage, wind speed or EF severity.
NDVI/NBR thresholds are predeclared exploratory diagnostics, not scientifically calibrated damage classes. Report all nine sensitivity combinations; never tune to NTP agreement.
2021 WorldCover tree cover can be stale or misclassified in 2025. The baseline NDVI criterion limits the study population, not all forest or all tornado-affected land.

The revised June 15–July 26 42-day baseline is farther from the event and asymmetric with the 21-day comparison. Phenology/leaf development, moisture, illumination, logging, other wind, fire and cloud/shadow can cause change; this is a stronger temporal confound than the failed original 21-day baseline.

Each 20 m cell mixes vegetation and surroundings. RGB/indices are medians of daily observations, not a simultaneous photograph; per-pixel first/last contributing dates and distinct clear-date counts are retained.

The original July 6–26 baseline failed its unchanged 80% mapped-forest coverage requirement (35.959%). V2 is an explicitly documented one-time baseline revision; quality/count/coverage/indicator thresholds are unchanged, and no search or automatic relaxation occurs.

Unobserved or ineligible land is not unchanged or undamaged. Two clear-date and two coverage gates still fail closed; original-window count/support rasters and per-date forest coverage are diagnostic, not evidence that V2 succeeds.
NTP independently documents the event using satellite review including Sentinel imagery. It is contextual corroboration of observability, not independent pixel-level validation of this experiment.

As checked 22 October 2026, NTP's current public Damage Tracks service does not contain a full Law Lake line. Do not synthesize a line or footprint from published start/end coordinates, maximum width or a map image.
